about: Command-line programs (DESIGN 5.20). `program` is what a generated program hands its runtime: its name, its help, and its commands in the order they are declared, each with its `line` (the words typed, hyphenated), its help, its arguments and its options. Kinds: text, integer, decimal, money, date, datetime, duration, enum (with its `values`) and, for options, bool. Values given and read are text, so decimals stay exact; null is the empty value of the kind. `words` are Clarity's own words of the command line (translations CLI_KEYS) in English, as a program shows them without a translation; `{name}` is a slot. `parse` gives what a command line becomes: `run` (the command and every argument's and option's value: as read, the option's default when it is left out, false for a bool, null for one without a default), `help` (the text written to standard output, exit code 0), or `wrong` (the message as a key and its slots, and the text written to standard error, exit code 2). The words after the program's name are read one by one: `help` first asks for help on what follows; a word that is no command or group is wrong; a group alone shows its help; `--help` anywhere shows the help of the command or group read so far; `--name value` and `--name=value` give an option, a bool option is a flag (`--vip`, or `--vip=true` and `--vip=false`); `--` ends the options; every other word is the next argument. An option given twice keeps the last. Numbers are written with a dot and no groups, as in scripts; dates as 2026-10-23, moments as 2026-10-23T14:30 or with seconds, durations as formats.json reads them (3:45, 1:02:03, or seconds alone), enum values by their name in any case. A number past its `min` or `max` is wrong. Messages are checked in this order: unknown command, unknown option, an option without its value, a value that is not of its kind, past min or max, a missing argument, too many arguments, a required option left out. Help: a description line (none for a group) and an empty line; the usage line; then sections, each a heading line and lines indented by two spaces with the left column padded to the longest in that section plus two spaces; sections apart by an empty line; trailing spaces never written. An option's line shows `--name <name>` (`--name` alone for a bool), then its help and, in parentheses, its marks joined by `; `: its enum values joined by `, `, `default X`, `required`. A wrong command line writes its message, then the usage line of the command or group read so far (the program's when none). `table` gives what `print list columns a, b` writes: a line of headings, then a line per row, the columns two spaces apart, each as wide as its longest cell, a column of numbers aligned right (its heading too) and the rest left, no trailing spaces. `ask` gives how a command asks on a terminal: the prompt written (no line end), the lines typed (null is the end of input), and the answer given, or the exit code when there is none: a yes or no prompt shows its two words in brackets and takes either word in any case, an empty line or the end of input is a no; a value prompt shows its default in brackets, an empty line takes the default, a line that is not of the kind writes the wrong-answer message and asks again, the end of input ends the program with exit code 1; a choice lists numbered lines and asks for a number. Without a terminal (`terminal` false) a question with a default gives it at once and writes nothing, and one without ends with exit code 2 and the no-terminal message.
